_comment: Prepared, not run (#11's own text: 'Publish conformance evidence for both collections and a bounded compatibility statement; do not build a second large benchmark'). Execution needs a --subject flag that materializes the named subject through materialize.py, installs it via DockerBackend.install() into a real container, observes discovery via the client's own no-model listing (the same codex debug prompt-input path skillc/exposure.py already uses), and re-verifies an in-container digest against the installation receipt (orchestrator ruling, msg 1474/1479) - never a model call. As of msg 1488 (w1), this is being split OUT of #81/#97 into its own follow-up PR under #11, since #97's own --subject shape (materialize-only, no container install) predates that ruling and is not being widened to match it. #81's lifecycle and grading demos are unaffected either way: slug-small-fix stays the graded task regardless of --subject. Neither the follow-up PR nor #10's own live Docker run exists yet.

acceptance_status._comment: Orchestrator ruling (msg 1479, relayed from the operator): the no-agent demo this manifest prepares gives per-collection INSTALLATION and DISCOVERY conformance against a real daemon - an in-container digest check against the receipt, plus the client's own listing. It does NOT satisfy bullet 2, which needs an agent actually working the Level 1 task with each collection installed - a real model call this manifest deliberately never makes.
acceptance_status.bullet_1_selection_provenance_license: MET - evals/subjects/mattpocock-skills/SUBJECT.md (#71/#11): independently authored, different layout, compatible capability scope, provenance and licence recorded
acceptance_status.bullet_2_same_client_fixture_contract_gr: NOT MET by this manifest alone - installation and discovery conformance only. Needs an agent working evals/level1/slug-small-fix with each collection installed, through the SAME client/contract/grader - a real model call, owed to the operator's live run. Funding basis (operator ruling, verbatim, msg 1481): "Normal Claude and codex" - the operator's own normal Claude Code and Codex subscription logins, inside the normal usage budget, NOT metered API spend and NOT gated by the #12 $5 cost stop (that ruling covers judge calls only, e.g. mcp-second-opinion, which use provider API keys). Needs #98 (subscription credential injection into a trial container) first.
acceptance_status.bullet_3_no_branch_refused_before_select: MET - tests/test_materialize.py's genericity guard (CORE_MODULES, an open set since #94) and test_a_malformed_subject_declaration_is_refused's 10 parametrized cases; cited, not re-proven here
acceptance_status.bullet_4_conformance_evidence_and_compat: PARTIALLY MET - this manifest's own runs, once executed, give installation+discovery conformance evidence for both collections through a real daemon; the compatibility statement below is bounded to state exactly that scope, not more
acceptance_status.what_remains_after_this_manifest_s_own_r: ONE item: an agent run on evals/level1/slug-small-fix, once per collection, with that collection's selected skills installed - a real, costed model call. #11 stays open until that happens; this manifest's own runs do not close it by themselves.

bounded_compatibility_statement: See README.md in this directory for the full statement, which keeps three kinds of claim separate: executed evidence (materialize.py has actually run against both subjects on the host), static proof (trial.py/verify.py/backend.py/docker_backend.py carry no subject-name branch, never demonstrated by execution), and what remains unshown by either - a full trial (plan, dispatch, capture, grade) for either subject through any backend, AND an agent actually working Level 1 with either collection installed (bullet 2, a real model call). This manifest's own two runs, once executed, close the first gap (installation+discovery through a real daemon) but not the second - #11 stays open until an agent run happens, on the operator's normal Claude Code/Codex subscription login per their own ruling ("Normal Claude and codex", msg 1481), not metered spend and not gated by the #12 cost stop (that covers judge calls only), and needing #98's credential injection first. This says NOTHING about which collection helps an agent more, about task outcomes, or about any paid model call already having happened.
